html:
The Emergency was a period of twenty-one months, from June 1975 to March 1977, when the prime minister Indira Gandhi ruled India by decree. It is the only break in Indian democracy since 1947.

On 12 June 1975 a court found her guilty of breaking election rules in 1971 and barred her from office. A protest movement led by the old Gandhian Jayaprakash Narayan was already calling on her to go. On the night of 25 June she had the president declare a state of emergency.

Before dawn the opposition leaders were arrested and the electricity to Delhi's newspaper offices was cut. Over the next months:

  • more than 100,000 people were held without trial;
  • the press was censored;
  • elections were put off, and Parliament changed the constitution to shield her.

Her son Sanjay, who held no office, ran two campaigns of his own. Slums in Delhi were bulldozed. More than eight million people, mostly poor men, were sterilised in a single year, many under pressure or by force.

In January 1977 she called an election, perhaps believing she would win. She lost her own seat, and Congress lost power for the first time. She returned in 1980. The constitution was changed so that an emergency is far harder to declare.
sum: The Emergency was a period of twenty-one months, from June 1975 to March 1977, when the prime minister Indira Gandhi ruled India by decree. It is the only break in Indian democracy since 1947.
